Knowledge of Product

Beyond the Mandate

Compliance gets us in the door. It's not the only reason we're in the room.

🗝️

"Private company" often gets read as "no need" — no filing, no deadline, no urgency. It's the wrong read. Underneath the regulatory pitch, this platform solves real coordination pain, filing or not — and two customers with zero filing obligations prove it.

Screen 1 · What We Actually Solve For

Six Value Drivers

Notice none of these mention a regulator.

⚙️

Before talking about who we sell to, it helps to know what the platform actually does for anyone using it, regulated or not:

Speed
40% faster last-mile reporting. Close sooner, publish first.
Transparency
Board, regulators, investors, whoever's watching, all see the same truth at the same time.
Accuracy
Structured data. Zero version chaos. Every number reconciled, not re-typed.
Auditability & Accountability
Every number and action is 100% traceable — what makes accountability enforceable, not aspirational.
Co-ordination & Control
Multiple teams, working off one single source of truth, instead of six spreadsheet versions.
Productivity
Fewer hours spent wrangling data, more hours spent making decisions with it.
Read that list again. Not one of these six requires a regulator to exist. That's the whole point of this module.
Screen 2 · Why We Focus Here First

Why Listed Companies Are The Sweet Spot

Real reasons, not just habit.

🎯

Listed companies aren't the sweet spot by accident. They have the pain in its most acute form: multiple teams — finance, legal, sustainability, investor relations — all touching the same numbers, on a real deadline, with real penalties for missing it.

Think back to BANT from Funnel Vision: a regulatory mandate hands a prospect Need and Timeline before the call even starts. That's what makes listed companies the fastest, most efficient place to sell — the forcing function already exists. We don't have to create urgency, it's already sitting there.

This is why the sales motion focuses here first. It is not the reason to stop here.
Screen 3 · The Part Most People Miss

The Need Doesn't Stop At The Regulatory Line

Version chaos doesn't check anyone's listing status.

🚧

The six value drivers on the last screen don't require a regulator to be true. Any company with more than one team touching the same report has version chaos, coordination problems, and manual reconciliation, whether or not anyone's filing anything with anyone.

A private company never has to publish a 10-K. It still closes its books every quarter. It still has a board that wants one clean number. It still has teams burning hours reconciling spreadsheets by hand. That pain doesn't wait for a listing to show up.

The instinct to check is "do they have a filing requirement?" That's the wrong first question. The better one is on the next-to-last screen of this module — hold that thought.
Screen 4 · Not Theory

Real Companies, Real Proof

Two companies, zero filing requirements, real business.

🏭
Miba Group · Austria

A private, family-owned industrial group with zero public disclosure obligation. They raised an RFP for IRIS anyway, for internal reporting, because the process pain (coordination across teams, one source of truth) was reason enough on its own.

Sammons · United States

Another private company we're actively working with, also for internal reporting, also with no regulatory filing driving it.

Neither company needed us to comply with anything. They needed to stop losing hours to manual reconciliation and version chaos. That's the same six value drivers from Screen 1, just with no regulator in the room.
Screen 5 · The Better Question

What This Means For You

Change the question, not just the answer.

💭

The instinct to check is: "do they have a filing requirement?"

The better instinct is: "do multiple teams touch the same numbers, and is that currently painful?"

A private company answering "yes, that's genuinely a mess right now" is a real conversation, not a dead end. Don't let "they're private" end the conversation before it even starts.
